text: Let's make a notebook reusable instead of one-off — widgets and parameters.

Reading one specific month's file works fine, once. But running the same logic for February means editing the string by hand — exactly the one-off thinking Foundations Lesson 27's ETL capstone deliberately avoided.

D-butils dot widgets dot text adds an input box at the top of the notebook, with a default value and a label. Get reads whatever's currently in it, always as a string. Change the box, rerun the notebook, and the same logic runs against different data — no code edits at all.

This matters most for job clusters. A human running a notebook interactively can just edit the code directly. But a job cluster has no human present — Databricks jobs pass widget values as parameters at run time instead. That's how one parameterized notebook becomes a building block a schedule can run every day.
Text, dropdown, combobox, multiselect — four types, one way to read them back. Next lesson: Databricks Runtime and versions, what's actually running underneath a cluster.
